class.name: EretheaMotionBlur
class.brief_description: Motion blur for moving objects and for the camera.
class.description: A [CompositorEffect] that blurs each pixel along its motion since the previous frame, from the renderer's motion vectors, so both moving objects and camera movement are blurred. Add it to a [Compositor] and set that compositor on a [WorldEnvironment] or a [Camera3D]. Put it before an [EretheaPostEffect] in [member Compositor.compositor_effects], so the film grain isn't blurred. The sky, which has no motion vectors, is blurred with the camera's rotation. Something that stays still on screen in front of a moving background, such as a character the camera follows, isn't smeared over that background. The blur is drawn after the transparent pass, before temporal antialiasing, upscaling and tone mapping. Asking for motion vectors has a cost of its own when neither TAA nor FSR 2 is on. [b]Note:[/b] This effect needs the Forward+ renderer. With the Mobile and Compatibility renderers it does nothing. [b]Note:[/b] [member CompositorEffect.effect_callback_type] and the buffer settings of [CompositorEffect] don't apply to this effect, which always runs after the transparent pass with the motion vectors.

members.member: Fraction of the frame during which the virtual shutter is open: [code]0.5[/code] blurs along half of each pixel's motion between two frames, like a film camera's 180° shutter. [code]0.0[/code] turns it off.
Longest blur, as a fraction of the screen width, so very fast motion doesn't smear the whole screen.
Number of samples along each pixel's motion. More samples give smoother long blurs and cost more.
